Use both qualitative and quantitative evaluation, both are essential.

The qualitative evaluation is essential for understanding: to define the scope of open questions, for designing and interpreting quantitative work.

While the quantitative evaluation is essential for generalization, to go beyond the data that a single person can understand at once, and estimate the confidence about how well the patterns in the numbers are really representative or reliable with respect to the outside world.

For that really to work, you need to be careful about the quantitative design and do it from multiple perspectives too.

All of this, these are all estimates and "all models are wrong, but some are useful."

Even the best evaluation is not perfect, each step is getting closer, getting a better perspective.
